children: Japan's economic performance in the third quarter probably won't prevent the BOJ from raising rates in December, says Capital Economics' Marcel Thieliant. Indeed, it seems increasingly likely that the BOJ will have to tighten policy more aggressively than expected as inflation is about to surge. While the GDP print was rather discouraging it was hardly a disaster, the economist says. Growth is set to overshoot the BOJ's median forecast of a 0.7% on quarter rise across the fiscal year started in April even if output remains stagnant over the next couple of quarters, CE says. Plus, the BOJ tankan survey indicates the most favorable business conditions since the early-1990s. Accordingly, CE still expects a rate hike in December. (fabiana.negrinochoa@wsj.com)
